decisions_this_run: D-068a: compare the approval's recorded `required_approvals` against the CALL's threshold at lookup time, rather than re-deriving the row's threshold or trusting `is_usable`. `is_usable` answers 'was this row satisfied?', a different question from 'is this row enough for what I am about to do?'.

D-068b: the guard is `>=`, a floor, not `==`. An approval granted under a stricter rule must stay spendable under a relaxed one; requiring equality would make relaxing a policy invalidate approvals already granted, forcing humans to re-approve for no security gain.

D-068c: did not fix it in the SQL spend guard. That predicate also compares against the row's own weaker `required_approvals`, so it cannot see the mismatch; the correction belongs where the call's threshold is known, which is the use case.

D-068d: on the checkpoint conflict, based the file on the concurrent run's version rather than overwriting it, because that version carries real delivery evidence (PR #5 body updated, issue #2 comment 7228642936) that this run did not produce. Discarding it would have reported delivery work as undone.
run_summary: NEX-068 closes a verified fail-open in the tool gateway's approval lookup. `_approved_request` matched an approval on capability, resource and `is_usable` but never compared the threshold the row was opened under against the threshold the current call requires, so a one-signature grant stayed spendable after the policy was tightened to two: the two-person control was bypassable by timing. The lookup now takes the call's `required_approvals` and treats a weaker row as unusable, leaving the strict approval to the existing deferral path, which is the only path that asks a human again. The guard is a floor, so a grant that met a stricter rule stays valid. Proved the new tests catch the defect by removing only the guard line: both negative tests failed with `DID NOT RAISE AccessDenied` because the single signature executed the delete. Gates on the merged tree: ruff format/check clean, mypy clean (140 files), 1444 passed / 4 skipped. A concurrent run had also edited tools.py (NEX-066) in a different region, so the change applied onto f8ae00c with no conflict and every gate was re-run afterwards. COMMITTED + PUSHED, NOT YET CI-POLLED. Honest note: the checkpoint ranked NEX-067 (AMR factor independence) first and the coordinator summary named NEX-065; neither was started, and NEX-067 remains the top priority.

head_drift_policy: `commit` names the last head whose *product* code was verified by CI, not necessarily the branch tip. NEXUS checkpoint updates are themselves docs-only commits, so the tip advances one commit past `commit` every time this file is written - chasing it is an unbounded loop (run 64 hit this: 7456a89 -> 974d03f -> c49befe, each fix creating a new tip). On reconciliation, compare the product tree, not the SHA: `git diff <commit>..HEAD -- src/ tests/` being empty means `commit` is still an accurate description of what CI verified.
commit_note: A checkpoint commit cannot name itself. 787ed57 is the last substantive commit; every later commit on this branch is a docs-only checkpoint that descends from it, so its CI still compiles and tests the same product code. To find the live head, poll `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/feature/agentic-enterprise-platform` rather than trusting this field. Each such docs commit also cancels the previous head's in-flight CI (branch concurrency), so `conclusion: cancelled` means superseded, never failed.
